profile.campus: San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas (QTS San Antonio 2 campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, San Antonio 2 sits at 8535 Potranco Road, San Antonio, TX 78251 on a 32-acre campus with 90+ MW of power capacity; no individual building/data-hall names or sqft figures are published.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built data center capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model it shares with peers such as Digital Realty and CyrusOne. Since Blackstone completed its roughly $10 billion take-private acquisition in August 2021, QTS has continued expanding across multiple US metros rather than slowing development, including major campus filings and expansions in Phoenix (a 750MW, 375-acre Glendale campus acquired for $255.3 million in July 2022) and Dallas-Fort Worth (its two mega-scale Irving and Fort Worth campuses), consistent with the scale of buildout QTS has also pursued in Northern Virginia, Georgia, and Ohio, tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS was originally founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas by Chad Williams, and grew through a mix of acquisitions and ground-up construction into a national wholesale/colocation platform before its 2013 IPO as a publicly traded REIT; that public period ended with the 2021 Blackstone take-private deal. QTS's current published portfolio language describes over 30 facilities across North America and Europe on its own site, while Wikipedia gives a somewhat different approximate figure of 28 locations across 16 US states plus two Netherlands sites (Eemshaven and Groningen), a discrepancy this registry notes rather than resolves in favor of either source.

reading.body:
QTS San Antonio II occupies 32 acres in San Antonio with 90+ MW of published power capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this supports roughly 2,250 racks. The campus sits in Texas alongside 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 18 publish power figures totaling 468 MW, making this facility unpublished in the current ranking though the operator claims sufficient scale to matter at regional level.

The facility is a wholesale colocation campus, meaning it leases built capacity to enterprise and hyperscale tenants rather than operating end-user services. QTS positions itself as hyperscale-neutral across its portfolio of over 30 North American and European sites, a business model consistent with its ownership by Blackstone through its real estate income trust following the take-private acquisition completed in August 2021. No certifications, security standards, or specific grid interconnection details are published for this campus on the operator's specification page.

The 90+ MW figure places this facility within the top regional tier for Texas but below the scale of QTS's marquee campuses in Phoenix and the Dallas-Fort Worth belt. The absence of building-level specifications, cooling architecture details, or planned expansion timelines on the published page limits what grid and connectivity planning this campus enables for external stakeholders. Whether this represents a mature, stable operation or a candidate for expansion cannot be read from the published facts.
